$comment: RELEASED MANIFEST CONTENT, ONE ENTRY PER VERSION. Maintained by hand, checked by src/version-lockstep.test.ts.

Each value is sha256 of block.manifest.json with the `version` key REMOVED and the remaining keys serialised in sorted order — i.e. a fingerprint of everything the store reads EXCEPT the version itself.

WHY: `civitai app submit` refuses a version that is not strictly above the highest APPROVED one, so changing what the manifest says without bumping the version produces a change that CAN NEVER SHIP, and nothing else in the repo notices. It has happened twice on this repo's main: dde1a6c re-wrote 0.2.0's manifest, and 4dbdff4 (PR #15) added `bootSkeleton: true` while leaving 0.3.2 in place — that skeleton sat un-shippable on main while production kept serving the earlier 0.3.2 tree.
0.3.2 records the tree that was actually APPROVED and served (05cdbbf, PR #14), not 4dbdff4's rewrite of it. Recording the rewrite would be recording the defect as if it were a release.

Several versions share a hash on purpose: a release that changes only app code leaves the manifest's content identical, and that is legitimate. The guard is ONE-directional — content changed => the version must be new.
TO CUT A RELEASE: bump `version` in BOTH block.manifest.json and package.json, then add the new version here. The test prints the exact line to add when it fails.
